lyrics:
[Intro: lonely electric guitar, sparse piano]

[Verse 1: gritty male voice, low]
Every time it got hard we said the same old thing
"We'll cross that bridge when we come to it," and kept driving
Money, your mother, the job out of state
We kicked it down the road, and the road ran out today

[Chorus: full band, raw and high]
So here's the bridge
Rusted rail, river running underneath
Your hand on the door, my foot on the brake
One of us has got to speak
We can turn around and lose what we had
Or cross that bridge and see what's on the other bank
I'm scared too. Take my hand.
Let's cross that bridge

[Verse 2: voice lower, guitar and piano]
It's the real one out on Miller Road, you know the one
Where I asked you, where you said yes, where we watched the sun
I drove us here on purpose. I don't have a speech.
I just couldn't do this in the kitchen, in the heat

[Chorus: full band, raw and high]
So here's the bridge
Rusted rail, river running underneath
Your hand on the door, my foot on the brake
One of us has got to speak
We can turn around and lose what we had
Or cross that bridge and see what's on the other bank
I'm scared too. Take my hand.
Let's cross that bridge

[Guitar Solo: slow, crying bends]

[Bridge: piano only, quiet]
My folks never crossed one. They just parked and stayed.
Forty years in the same front seat, looking the other way.

[Final Chorus: biggest, then a whisper on the last line]
So here's the bridge
Rusted rail, river running underneath
Your hand on the door, my foot on the brake
One of us has got to speak
We can turn around and lose what we had
Or cross that bridge and see what's on the other bank
I'm scared too. Take my hand.
Let's cross that bridge

[Outro: river sound, an engine shifts into drive]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 70 BPM, 4/4, E minor. A slow power ballad: hushed verses and a chorus that breaks open.

VOICE: Male, young-sounding but hoarse, with gravel on every held note. Quiet and close in the verses, pushed to the edge of cracking in the choruses. The final line is whispered.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar with reverb, piano, a second overdriven guitar in the choruses, bass, heavy slow drums, a pedal steel behind the choruses, strings in the last chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and piano. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:48 Chorus 1. 1:22 Verse 2. 1:56 Chorus 2. 2:30 Guitar solo. 2:46 Bridge, piano only. 3:04 Final chorus, ends on a whisper. 3:32 Outro, river and an engine in gear at 3:38.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2022 country power ballad: wide and dramatic, big reverb on the drums, the voice raw and loud.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The whispered last 'Let's cross that bridge' at 3:28, followed by the engine going into drive.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original leaves a young couple stuck. This one makes a decision: an older man who watched his parents avoid the talk for forty years puts the car in gear.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Avoidance, facing it, fear said aloud, forward.
